root_cause.text: In pseries/papr-hvpipe, papr_hvpipe_handle_read() copied a stack-allocated struct papr_hvpipe_hdr to userspace after only partially initializing it, leaving reserved padding fields uninitialized and causing kernel stack data disclosure.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that “hdr variable is allocated on the stack and only hdr.version and hdr.flags are initialized explicitly,” while papr_hvpipe_hdr contains “reserved[3] and reserved2[40]” bytes that “could leak the uninitialized bytes to userspace after copy_to_user(),” and the patch fixes this by changing `struct papr_hvpipe_hdr hdr;` to `struct papr_hvpipe_hdr hdr = {};`.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit states that “hdr variable is allocated on the stack and only hdr.version and hdr.flags are initialized explicitly,” while papr_hvpipe_hdr contains “reserved[3] and reserved2[40]” bytes that “could leak the uninitialized bytes to userspace after copy_to_user(),” and the patch fixes this by changing `struct papr_hvpipe_hdr hdr;` to `struct papr_hvpipe_hdr hdr = {};`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Zero-initialize the hvpipe header in papr_hvpipe_handle_read() to avoid use of uninitialized stack data.
intent_record.what: The local variable declaration in papr_hvpipe_handle_read() was changed from `struct papr_hvpipe_hdr hdr;` to `struct papr_hvpipe_hdr hdr = {};`, adding zero-initialization of the stack-allocated header structure at declaration.
intent_record.how: This ensures the `hdr` structure starts with all fields cleared before any later use, preventing runtime behavior from depending on uninitialized stack data if the structure is only partially filled before being read, copied, or passed onward.

grouping_result.intent: Zero-initialize the hvpipe header in papr_hvpipe_handle_read() to avoid use of uninitialized stack data.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause by zero-initializing the stack-allocated hvpipe header before copying it to userspace, preventing disclosure of uninitialized padding/reserved fields.

candidates.rationale: This stack-allocated header is declared without initialization. Because the function later copies this struct to userspace after only partial field initialization, any reserved or padding bytes in hdr can contain stale kernel stack data, causing information disclosure.

vuln_statements.explanation: This stack-allocated header is left uninitialized at declaration. The function later copies the struct to userspace after only partially setting fields, so reserved or padding bytes can leak stale kernel stack contents, matching the root cause.
